Question: Can agents identify patterns, interpret context, and make low-risk decisions without human intervention? Provide examples (e.g., auto-routing requests, flagging data inconsistencies).
Response: Yes. GHCP SDK agentic loops are autonomous by design — each session loads skills and MCP tools, reasons about the task, makes decisions, and executes. Autonomy is governed by configurable thresholds stored in the workflow state. Examples from our architecture: (1) Invoice triage — the agentic loop reads invoice data via Workday MCP, identifies three-way match status, and auto-approves invoices below a configurable threshold without human intervention. (2) CV screening — the agentic loop scores candidates against criteria defined in the screening skill, auto-shortlists candidates above 85% confidence, routes 60-85% to HR BP exception queue, and auto-rejects below 60%. (3) Data inconsistency detection — the validation skill flags duplicate invoices, mismatched PO numbers, or anomalous amounts and routes exceptions to the Fleet Manager's exception queue. Thresholds are adjustable at runtime via the Control Plane without redeployment.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK agentic loops, skills, configurable autonomy thresholds
POC Demo: POC1: Show invoice auto-approval for low-risk items vs routing high-value invoices to Finance BP. POC2: Show CV auto-shortlisting with configurable confidence thresholds.

Question: Can agents decompose complex, multi-step goals into sub-tasks and execute them across systems? Provide an example (e.g., 'Onboard employee X' spanning multiple systems).
Response: Yes. The architecture uses Azure Durable Functions for goal decomposition into phases, with GHCP SDK agentic loops executing each phase. Example: 'Hire a Senior Data Engineer in USA' decomposes into: (1) Budget check phase — agentic loop loads budget skill, calls Workday + Dataverse MCP tools, produces cost impact analysis. (2) Job design phase — agentic loop loads job-design skill, drafts role profile and JD from internal sources. (3) Sourcing phase (parallel with job design) — agentic loop loads sourcing skill, searches internal talent pool, posts to Greenhouse and LinkedIn via MCP. (4) Screening phase — agentic loop loads screening skill, parses CVs, scores candidates, shortlists. (5) Interview scheduling — loads scheduling skill, coordinates across timezones via Graph MCP. (6) Offer phase — loads offer skill, generates letter, routes for approval. (7) Onboarding — loads onboarding skill, triggers JML workflow via ServiceNow MCP. Each phase is an independent agentic loop that loads the right skills, executes across the required systems, writes state, and exits. Durable Functions coordinates sequencing, parallelism, and HITL waits between phases.
Key Technologies: Azure Durable Functions (orchestration), GHCP SDK (phase execution), MCP servers (system integration)
POC Demo: POC2: Full end-to-end hiring workflow from requisition to onboarding spanning Workday, Greenhouse, LinkedIn, Graph, ServiceNow.

Question: How do agents learn from past interactions, human feedback, and new data? Describe mechanisms for improving performance over time.
Response: Three learning mechanisms. (1) Episodic memory via workflow state store: the agentic loop writes outcomes to the workflow state store (Cosmos DB/Dataverse). Future loops can query past outcomes — e.g. recall that the last 3 hires for a similar role were levelled too low, adjusting compensation benchmarking accordingly. (2) Skill crystallisation: when an agentic pattern proves reliable (e.g. CV parsing logic), it graduates from LLM-generated reasoning to deterministic code, versioned as a skill in Azure API Center. This is learning encoded as capability — proven patterns become faster, cheaper, and more predictable over time. (3) Human feedback loop: when a human overrides an agent decision via the Control Plane (e.g. changes a shortlist recommendation), the override is logged with context. The Fleet Manager agent analyses override patterns and proposes skill or threshold adjustments. Process evolution: after completed workflows, the Fleet Manager detects friction points (e.g. works council notifications causing 3-day delays) and surfaces improvement proposals on the Control Plane for operator approval.
Key Technologies: Workflow state store (Cosmos DB), skill crystallisation (API Center), Fleet Manager agent
POC Demo: POC2: Show episodic memory — hiring agent recalls past levelling issues. Show Fleet Manager proposing process improvement after 10 completed workflows.

Question: How effectively can agents interpret natural language from emails, chat, and free-text fields? Describe generation capabilities for responses and summaries.
Response: GHCP SDK agentic loops use frontier LLMs from the Foundry model catalog for NLU/NLG. The agentic loop natively reasons over natural language inputs from any source — email content parsed via Graph MCP, Teams messages via M365 Agents SDK, free-text fields from business systems via MCP tools. NLU capabilities: intent extraction from emails (e.g. invoice dispute, hiring request), entity extraction (candidate names, amounts, dates, PO numbers), sentiment and urgency assessment, multi-language support via model capabilities. NLG capabilities: compose contextual email responses via the human's PA, generate structured summaries for Control Plane situational awareness, draft job descriptions, offer letters, and onboarding plans from templates enriched with workflow context. All generated content routes through the human's PA for review before outbound communication — the human decides, the PA prepares and executes.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK + Foundry model catalog, M365 Agents SDK, Graph MCP
POC Demo: POC2: Show email parsing of hiring manager request, automatic JD generation, and contextual summary generation for Control Plane drill-down.

Question: How are agents configured to interact with external APIs, databases, and connectors to perform actions in source systems? Describe the developer experience.
Response: The developer experience centres on two artefacts: skills and MCP servers. Skills (SKILL.md files) declaratively define what the agent can do — capabilities, allowed tools, governance rules. MCP servers expose enterprise systems as typed tools that agentic loops discover and invoke. Developer workflow: (1) Build an MCP server wrapping a REST API (or use APIM REST-to-MCP gateway for auto-generation from OpenAPI spec). (2) Register the MCP server in APIM AI Gateway with auth, rate limiting, and content safety policies. (3) Write a skill that declares which MCP tools it uses and what business logic governs their invocation. (4) Register the skill in Azure API Center with lifecycle management. (5) The agentic loop loads the skill, discovers available MCP tools, reasons about the task, and invokes tools as needed. All tool calls are governed by APIM policies and intercepted by GHCP SDK session hooks. Pro-code in Python or TypeScript. The entire configuration is Git-committable — skills as markdown, MCP server code, APIM policies as code.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (Python/TypeScript), MCP servers, APIM REST-to-MCP gateway, Azure API Center, SKILL.md
POC Demo: POC1: Walk through building a custom Maconomy MCP server from OpenAPI spec and registering it in APIM.
